completeMeaning: All 213 frozen web paths underwent the declared structural/content inspection and user-path review. This is not a claim that every source/test line received a manual full-text reading; exact manual full-text and structural-only coverage are recorded separately.
releaseGate: failed: 3 reproduced functional/usability findings; not a clean audit

findings.title: Creating a project leaves the next message targeted at the previous project
findings.scenario: With Old Project already selected, create New Project using the new-project dialog. The dialog closes without selecting the returned ID or retaining a success-target notice. The old project remains selected; the next ordinary message dispatches conversation/start with projectId old.
findings.impact: The primary create-project/start-work flow can send intended new-project work into an existing directory or old thread.

evidence.observed: New Project appears, Old Project remains selected, and the captured conversation/start params.projectId is old.

findings.recommendation: Return the accepted project ID to Workspace, refresh the registered list, and explicitly hand off to a new chat in that project while retaining the prior draft and respecting navigation changes.

findings.title: Automation model selection loses provider identity
findings.scenario: Enable two providers that advertise model shared, with A supporting high and B supporting max. The automation editor emits both options with value/key shared, uses the first provider's reasoning list, reads defaults using model alone, and saves options {model:'shared'} without the intended provider.
findings.impact: The automation editor cannot distinguish same-name models, cannot reliably configure a nondefault provider, and may preserve an old provider when an existing automation changes its model.

evidence.observed: Both provider options have value shared; high is offered, max is absent; saved automation/create.spec.options contains only model. React also reports duplicate shared keys.

findings.recommendation: Use provider-plus-model identity for selection, persist modelProvider, fetch defaults with that provider, resolve effort against that exact catalog entry, and carry provider identity through collaboration mode preparation.

findings.title: Existing-thread settings use another provider's model capabilities
findings.scenario: Open execution settings for thread B whose session snapshot says shared/provider-b. Pass the merged catalog with provider A's shared/high first and provider B's shared/max second. The form offers A's high, omits B's max, and allows thread/settings/update{threadId:'thread-b',effort:'high'}. It also lists models belonging only to other providers.
findings.impact: A valid provider-B reasoning setting becomes unavailable, and the UI admits overrides that do not belong to the actual thread provider.

evidence.observed: Snapshot shared/provider-b is visible while high is offered and max is absent; captured settings update sends high to thread-b.

findings.recommendation: Pass snapshot.modelProvider into the form, filter models to that provider including supported legacy aliases, and validate model/effort/serviceTier using only the matching provider entry.

method.inventory: Frozen snapshot names restricted to web/**, excluding generated untracked web/dist. All 213 files were read from this clean-room repository; no old archive, history, personal home, credentials, deployment, commercial inference, or external MCP was used.
method.structural: TypeScript 7 local compiler API parsed all TS/TSX/MJS files and traversed every AST node. The retained evidence includes imports, test declaration expressions, assertion counts, focused/skipped declarations, RPC method/argument text, complete effect text, JSX event-handler text and function declarations. All file-level RPC/effect summaries and test scenario names were reviewed; this is structural inspection, not a claim of manual full-test-body reading.
method.manual: Full-text reading for the files in manualFullTextFiles; selected source ranges and cross-component call-flow review for the remaining production files. Core paths covered authentication/MFA, project creation and navigation, composer/models/provider settings, defaults and effort validation, usage, receipts and storage, background reconnect and terminal ownership, rendering, draft recovery, automation/execution settings, file/Git/worktree operations, MCP and extensions.
method.tests: Exactly one temporary local-protocol-substitute reproduction file, containing 3 specific defect reproductions, was executed. Final result: 3 passed (these assertions prove current incorrect behavior). An initial automation reproduction used an incorrect fixture button label; correcting that label produced the final pass. No product test was edited and no full suite or production build was run.
method.cssAndBuild: All eight CSS files and web build/bootstrap/configuration files were read. No current real-browser pixel/OS-IME/production-authentication/live-provider validation is claimed.
method.digest: node scripts/snapshot.mjs rechecked the original 1937-file digest at the end; unchanged.

limitations: Not all 213 source/test files received manual line-by-line full-text reading; structural inspection and focused control-flow review are explicitly distinguished.
No full suite, production build, commercial inference, real external MCP, live account credentials, production deployment, or real-browser screenshot session was performed in this audit.
